description:
Hi! I am Federico, an engineer and an audiovisual and technology enthusiast passionate about combining science, sound design, and software development.

Through GeoBeats, our goal is to push our creativity and bring to life innovative ideas on how NASA satellite imagery can be translated into music and immersive soundscapes, making Earth science accessible and engaging for everyone, including blind and visually impaired users.
summary:
GeoBeats (Earth Information Jukebox) is an interactive, accessible web platform that transforms NASA satellite imagery and Earth observation data into harmonic music and real-time soundscapes. While NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) produces extraordinary visualizations of climate, oceans, and the biosphere, purely visual science leaves out blind and visually impaired people.

GeoBeats bridges this gap by translating pixel luminance and RGB/HSV spectral values into musical notes across selectable diatonic Major and Minor scales (C, D, E, F, G, A, B), accompanied by a low-volume generative harmonic background soundtrack and six musical styles (Cosmic Chiptune, Deep Atmosphere, Solar Synthwave, Earth Jazz, Orbital Rock, and Cinematic). Featuring an automatic spoken audio guide for blind users, full keyboard navigation, scientific descriptions for each satellite dataset, and an instant bilingual interface (English/Spanish), GeoBeats empowers everyone to hear, explore, and feel the living pulse of our planet.
details:
WHAT GEOBEATS DOES AND HOW IT WORKS GeoBeats is an interactive Earth Information Jukebox designed to translate satellite datasets from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) and EOSDIS into harmonic musical compositions in real time. Its sonification engine operates through a three-layer scientific and musical pipeline:

  1. Physical and Spectral Mapping (RGB/HSV to Music):
  • Luminance to Musical Pitch: Darker regions (deep abyssal oceans, shadowed valleys) generate deep bass notes, while high-reflectance or high-intensity areas (glacier ice, thermal anomalies, fast ocean currents) produce higher-pitched notes.
  • Color to Timbre and Physical Biome Classification: Real-time chromatic analysis automatically identifies Earth features (Abyssal and Coastal Ocean, Biomass and Rainforest, Thermal Anomaly and Wildfire, Glacier Ice and Snow, and Arid Soil and Bedrock), dynamically shaping synthesizer envelopes and filter cutoffs.
  1. Selectable Diatonic Harmony and Generative Background Soundtrack:
  • Unlike traditional data sonifiers that produce harsh, isolated beeps out of silence, GeoBeats uses full 7-note diatonic Major (Ionian) and Natural Minor (Aeolian) scales across all 12 musical keys (defaulting to C Major), selectable in real time by the user.
  • It features a continuous, low-volume Harmonic Backing Soundtrack (with independent volume sliders for interactive notes and background harmony) that plays evolving diatonic chord progressions (I-V-vi-IV in Major and i-VI-III-VII in Minor) synchronized with the active key and modulated by low-frequency oscillators (LFOs) so every note blends smoothly.
  1. Two Exploration Modes and 6 Musical Personalities (Sound Packs):
  • Touch DJ Mode: Hovering or clicking anywhere on the satellite map uses a 3x3 spatial smoothing kernel and dynamic portamento to play notes smoothly while displaying live geographic coordinates (Latitude and Longitude), RGB values, note names, and frequencies.
  • Live Satellite Scanner Mode: A laser scanline sweeps across the planet like a musical sequencer synced to the user’s chosen tempo (BPM), sampling Northern, Equatorial, and Southern latitudes.
  • 6 Sound Packs: Cosmic Chiptune (8-bit retro), Deep Atmosphere (Lo-Fi and Ambient), Solar Synthwave (Analog Cyberpunk), Earth Jazz (Warm Rhodes), Orbital Rock (Harmonic Overdrive), and Cinematic (Orchestral Strings).

ACCESSIBILITY FOR BLIND AND VISUALLY IMPAIRED USERS AND EXPECTED IMPACT A core priority for our team was meaningful inclusion for blind and low-vision users:

  • Automatic Spoken Audio Guide (Web Speech API): As soon as the page opens, a voice narrator welcomes blind users, explains how touching or sliding across the screen translates dark and bright regions into low and high pitches, and reads a concise 1-paragraph scientific introduction for the active satellite map.
  • Hands-Free Keyboard Control: Pressing any letter key (A-Z) immediately stops the voice narration or restarts it from the very beginning; pressing the Spacebar starts or stops the automatic satellite scanner.
  • Instant Bilingual Interface (EN / ES): A flag toggle switches all UI controls, telemetry labels, musical notation (C4 vs Do4), scientific descriptions, and voice synthesis between English and Spanish in real time.
  • Custom Map Upload: Users and educators can also upload their own satellite maps or images to sonify them instantly.
  • Future Assistive Hardware Integration for Blind Users: As the next milestone in our roadmap, GeoBeats will incorporate dedicated physical and tactile hardware support for blind and visually impaired users. This includes integration with haptic feedback controllers and vibration wearables (translating thermal intensity, elevation, and ocean currents into physical vibrations), refreshable tactile pin-matrix and Braille displays to feel continental boundaries and topographic relief under the fingertips, and physical MIDI/rotary control surfaces with raised Braille markers so blind explorers can navigate coordinates, switch NASA datasets, and control musical scales entirely through touch and sound without needing a screen.
